column1: # The Dynamo parity exclusions (E11-T23 step B, DYNAMO-COVERAGE §7).
# The reverse direction of the parity manifest: of every public member of Spark.Geometry, either a
# row of dynamo-parity.tsv names it, or this file says why no row needs to. A member that is neither
# is counted against the residue budget at the foot of this file.
# IT EXCUSES BY RULE AND NEVER MEMBER BY MEMBER. Spark.Geometry declares 894 public members by the
# manifest's own counting rule - methods, properties, enum values and operators, and not constructors
# or property accessors, and 202 of the manifest's rows name one of them, naming 159 distinct members.
# 234 rows name a Spark member in all; the rest point at Spark.Api, Spark.Geometry.Io or
# Spark.Nodes.Core, which THIS direction does not read (E11-T30, E2-T45). Measured 2026-09-13 after
# E2-T46; the 895 and 130 this header carried before that day were stale and disagreed with
# DYNAMO-COVERAGE 7's own figure. A file of hand-written excuses for the hundreds left over would be the drifting artefact
# §7 exists to prevent. Two scopes do the work - a member-name rule that applies on any type, and a
# whole type Dynamo has no counterpart for - and what neither reaches is counted rather than waved
# through. 37 rules today: 5 member names and 32 types.
# A ROW MAY NAME A TYPE RATHER THAN A MEMBER, and a Done row legitimately does when the capability is a
# construction - Dynamo's Surface.ByRevolve is Spark's `new RevolutionSurface(...)`, and a constructor
# is not a member this inventory counts. Such a row claims the type, so the type may not then be
# excused here. Until 2026-09-12 naming a bare type slipped past that rule silently; E2-T42's
# assessment found it, and the check now catches it.
#   MemberName  Name is a member name, or op_* for the operators. Excused wherever it appears.
#   Type        Name is a full type name. Refused if any parity row names one of its members.
#   Budget      Name is "residue"; Reason begins with the count. The check requires an EXACT match,
#               so the number falls as rows are assessed and cannot quietly climb back.

299 members are named by no row and excused by no rule. Most sit on types that DO map to a Dynamo type, so each is either a member some Unassessed row will name once it is assessed or a genuine gap; a few are Spark's own machinery on a type a row names, which cannot be excused because the type is named, and are counted rather than argued away. The check requires an EXACT match, so the number falls as rows are assessed and cannot quietly climb back. THE HISTORY IS KEPT HERE, because a rise and a fall mean different things and neither should have to be guessed at. 278 to 287, 2026-09-12, E2-T44: assessing DYNAMO-COVERAGE 3.5 named 13 Spark members, which took BrepFaceView, BrepLoopView and BrepEdgeView out of the excused types and moved their remaining members here. 287 to 293, same day, E2-T65: BrepAdjacency arrived, 8 of its members named by rows and 6 not. 293 to 283, same day, E2-T42 step A: 11 more members named by Surface's rows - THE FIRST FALL, and the one the number exists to show. 283 to 291, same step: Surface.ByRevolve names the TYPE RevolutionSurface, because the capability is a constructor and constructors are not counted - so the type is claimed by a row, may no longer be excused wholesale, and its other members join the residue. 291 to 285, same day, E2-T42 step B: seven more members named by NurbsSurface's and PolySurface's rows. Unchanged at 285 through E11-T30 on 2026-09-12, which is the evidence that widening the RENAME-CATCHER to Spark.Api and Spark.Nodes.Core left this direction scoped to Spark.Geometry alone; and unchanged again through E2-T43, whose rows named BrepPrimitives.Box and Cylinder - taking that type off the excused list and adding nothing here, because those two are all it declares. 285 to 292, 2026-09-13, E2-T45: assessing DYNAMO-COVERAGE 3.6 both lowered this and raised it, and the rise is the larger half. Mesh's rows named 8 more of its members - Vertices, Normals, Faces, FaceCount, FaceNormal, Triangulated, Welded and TransformedBy - which took 8 off. But the rows also name MeshTopology.EdgeCount, MeshFace's corners and GeometryJson.Serialize, so those three types may no longer be excused wholesale, and their unnamed members came here: MeshTopology 9, MeshFace 5, GeometryJson 1, measured one at a time rather than reasoned about. A SECOND RISE OF THE E2-T42 KIND, and the same lesson - a type a row names is a type whose whole surface the register has to account for. 292 to 319, 2026-09-13, E2-T46: assessing DYNAMO-COVERAGE 3.8 named 3 more Spark.Geometry members - Curve.BoundingBox, PolyCurve.Segments and CoordinateSystem.ToTransform - and took TWO MORE TYPES off the excused list, Transform (28 unnamed members) and Tessellation (2), measured one at a time. THE BIGGEST SINGLE MOVE THIS NUMBER HAS MADE, and it is the true price of a claim rather than drift: 3.8's transformation family is Done BECAUSE Spark puts the whole transformation algebra on one type, so the moment six rows name Transform.Translation and its siblings, all 34 of Transform's members are the register's business. Excusing it wholesale while claiming it was the contradiction the check exists to catch. 319 to 321, 2026-09-13, E2-T70: Brep.TransformedBy and MeshFace.Reversed were added, and this is the FIRST RISE FROM NEW CODE rather than from an assessment - the check caught them on the first build after they were written, which is what it is for. They are counted rather than named, and deliberately: the parity rows for the transformation family name the Transform FACTORY, because 3.8's argument is that Spark has one mechanism where Dynamo repeats a member per type, so the per-type application members - Curve.TransformedBy, Surface.TransformedBy, Arc.TransformedBy and now Brep's - are counted here exactly as they always have been. MeshFace.Reversed is Mesh.TransformedBy's mirror handling and answers no Dynamo member of its own. 321 to 318, 2026-09-13, E2-T41 step A: assessing DYNAMO-COVERAGE 3.2's 82 Curve rows named 13 more Spark.Geometry members - Curve.PointAt, TangentAt, NormalAt, PlaneAt, CoordinateSystemAt, LengthAt, ParameterAtLength, PointAtLength, ClosestParameter, Domain, Trimmed, Reversed and PolyCurve.FromJoinedCurves - and took TWO MORE TYPES off the excused list: CurveOffset, because Curve.Offset names CurveOffset.Offset and its other two members (FilletLines, OffsetSamples) came here; and ExtrusionSurface, because Curve.Extrude names the TYPE for the reason Surface.ByRevolve names RevolutionSurface - a construction is a constructor and constructors are not counted - so its eight non-constructor members came here too. 13 off and 10 on. THE FIRST NET FALL SINCE E2-T42 step B, and the first from a section this size: a pass that names thirteen members of a type the register already watched buys more than it pays, where 3.8's pass claimed a type nobody had accounted for and paid 27. The difference is worth keeping in view when the remaining sections are planned, and is written up as N162. 318 to 303, 2026-09-13, E2-T41 step B: the ten concrete curve types, 105 rows, named 27 more Spark.Geometry members - Line's two factories, Arc's three and its Center, Circle's four and its Center, EllipseCurve's seven, NurbsCurve.InterpolatePoints, PolyCurve.SegmentCount, PolyLine's four factories and SegmentAt, and Plane.FromBestFit - and took ONE type off the excused list: Spark.Geometry.Planar.Region, because Polygon.Center names Region.Centroid and Polygon.ContainmentTest names Region.Contains, so its other 12 members are counted from today. It also names the bare type NurbsCurve, for the reason Surface.ByRevolve names RevolutionSurface - ByControlPoints is a constructor - which costs nothing here because NurbsCurve was never excused. 27 off and 12 on. THE LARGEST FALL THIS NUMBER HAS MADE, and N162 predicted the wrong sign: the note reasoned that a section of constructions would cost, and this section is almost nothing but constructions. What it missed is that Spark had ALREADY BUILT the curve factories, so the rows landed on members the assembly declares rather than on types nobody had accounted for. The rule survives, corrected: the cost is not whether the capabilities are constructions, it is whether the TYPES they construct were already in the register. 303 to 270, 2026-09-13, E2-T40: section 3.1's 78 remaining value rows named 33 more Spark.Geometry members - Plane's seven factories and its three world planes, CoordinateSystem's eight, BoundingBox's five, Vector3d's six, Point3d's four, Transform.Determinant and Transform.Multiply - and took NO type off the excused list, because every type this section touches was already claimed. The largest fall the number has made, and the cheapest kind of pass by N162 as corrected: rows landing on members of types the register already watched. It also names four BARE TYPES - Point3d, Vector3d, UV and Transform - for constructions that are constructors, and each costs nothing because none of the four was excused. THE RESIDUE IS NOW WHAT IT SAYS IT IS: with no Unassessed row left anywhere in the manifest, these 270 are no longer members some future assessment will name. Every one is either a genuine Spark capability with no Dynamo counterpart - which is most of them, and is the point of Spark - or a gap in the register. From here a RISE is the only thing that means anything, and it means exactly what this check was built to catch. 270 to 277, 2026-09-13, E2-T70 step B: curve/surface intersection arrived, and this is A RISE FROM NEW CODE - the second, after E2-T70 step A, and the first since the manifest had no Unassessed row left, which makes it the first rise this number could not have been hiding. The seven are CurveSurfaceIntersections' four members (None, Points, LiesOnSurface, IsEmpty) and CurveSurfaceIntersectionPoint's three (Point, Parameter, Uv); the Curve.IntersectWith OVERLOAD adds nothing, because the residue counts member names per type and that name was already there. They are counted rather than named, and for the same reason CurveIntersections and CurveOverlap are: Dynamo's Geometry.Intersect returns Geometry[], so there is no ProtoGeometry member for a RESULT TYPE to satisfy. The row they serve, Geometry.Intersect(Geometry), stays Planned because it has to answer every pair and surface/surface is still behind the seam. A rise with no entry here means a member was added to a mapped type with no thought for the register. 277 to 284, 2026-09-13, E2-T73: Helix arrived - the eighth curve type - and this is A RISE FROM NEW CODE, the third, and the second since the manifest had no Unassessed row left to hide one. The type declares FOURTEEN public members and this number rose by SEVEN, which is the whole arithmetic of the check working: six are named by the seven parity rows that moved from Planned to Done (FromAxis, AxisPoint, AxisDirection, Radius, Pitch, SweepAngle), ToString is excused by rule, and the seven counted here are the Curve OVERRIDES - Domain, IsClosed, LengthAt, ParameterAtLength, Reversed, Trimmed and TransformedBy. THAT IS EXACTLY WHAT CIRCLE AND ARC ALREADY CONTRIBUTE, member for member, and for the same reason: the parity rows for Curve's contract name Curve.Domain and Curve.LengthAt, because Spark puts the contract on the base class where Dynamo repeats it per type, so each concrete curve's override answers no Dynamo member of its own. A rise of seven on an eighth curve type is therefore the SAME PRICE the seven before it paid, and a rise of any other size would have meant the type had grown a member with no row behind it. 284 to 289, 2026-09-13, E2-T71 step A: Curve.ToNurbsCurve arrived with its result type, and this is A RISE FROM NEW CODE, the fourth. The five are NurbsConversion's two members (Curve, IsExact - ToString is excused by rule) and the three per-type OVERRIDES of ToNurbsCurve, on Line, PolyLine and NurbsCurve. Curve.ToNurbsCurve itself is NAMED by the row it satisfies and costs nothing. The overrides are counted for exactly the reason Curve.TransformedBy and Arc.TransformedBy are: the parity row names the member on the BASE, because Spark puts the contract on Curve where Dynamo repeats it per type, so an override answers no Dynamo member of its own. NurbsConversion is COUNTED RATHER THAN EXCUSED, and the precedent was split: CurveIntersections and CurveOverlap are excused Types, CurveSurfaceIntersections was counted by E2-T70 step B on the same stated reason. The later choice is followed deliberately - counting is the conservative direction, because a counted member is visible in this number and an excused one is invisible for ever, which is N163's argument for why the budget is exact rather than a ceiling. 289 to 292, 2026-09-13, E2-T71 step B: the rational conversions arrived and this is A RISE FROM NEW CODE, the fifth - three, and they are Arc.ToNurbsCurve, Circle.ToNurbsCurve and EllipseCurve.ToNurbsCurve. SAME REASON AS STEP A'S THREE, AND THE SAME REASON AS TransformedBy'S: the parity row names the member on the BASE, because Spark puts the contract on Curve where Dynamo repeats it per type, so an override answers no Dynamo member of its own. RationalArcs, which this step created, ADDS NOTHING HERE - it is internal, and the residue reads the public surface only. That is worth one line because it is the cheap shape: moving arithmetic into an internal helper is free in this number, and the six overrides across two steps are the whole price of putting a virtual on Curve. 292 to 300, 2026-09-13, E2-T71 family (2): planarity arrived and this is A RISE FROM NEW CODE, the sixth, and the largest of the six. Eight, and they are FOUR TYPES TIMES TWO MEMBERS: Line, Arc, Circle and EllipseCurve each override both IsPlanar and PlaneOf. Curve.IsPlanar and Curve.PlaneOf themselves are named by the rows they satisfy and cost nothing. SAME REASON AS EVERY OVERRIDE BEFORE THEM, and this is now the third consecutive step to pay it: the parity row names the member on the BASE, because Spark puts the contract on Curve where Dynamo repeats it per type, so an override answers no Dynamo member of its own. IT IS WORTH SEEING THE PATTERN RATHER THAN ONLY THE NUMBER: adding a virtual to Curve costs one residue per overriding type per member, and E2-T71 has now added three virtuals across three steps for six, three and eight. That is the price of a contract on a base class in a register built around a per-type inventory, it is not drift, and the alternative - naming the overrides in rows of their own - would be claiming eight Dynamo members that do not exist. 300 to 299, 2026-09-13, E2-T71 family (3): chord stepping and division from a parameter - AND THIS IS A FALL, WHICH IS NEW. Every fall before it came from an ASSESSMENT naming members that already existed; this one came from BUILDING. The two new member names, Curve.DivideByChordLength and Curve.DivideEquallyByChord, are each named by the row they satisfy and cost nothing - and Curve.DivideByLength, which had been sitting in this number unnamed since it was written, is now named by DivideByDistanceFromParameter and DivideByLengthFromParameter, because the overload that answers those rows shares its name. SO A STEP THAT ADDED PUBLIC API LOWERED THIS NUMBER, which sounds like a contradiction and is not: the residue counts members no row accounts for, and building the from-a-parameter form is what finally gave an old member a row to belong to. Worth keeping beside the six rises above it: a rise means a member arrived with no row behind it, a fall means a row arrived to account for one, and both happen while code is being written rather than only while it is being read.
